overview: The committee reviewed and refined a draft Request for Proposals (RFP) for a new zoning consultant to lead the next phase of the city’s zoning updates project. The council discussed selection oversight, the volume of public meetings, and amended the scope regarding design standards before authorizing the Planning Director to proceed with the procurement.

items.title: Introduction of Draft RFP and Procurement Process
items.summary: Director of Planning Alicia Hunt presented a draft RFP for a new zoning consultant and explained that the city would use a qualifications-based selection process rather than a low-bid model. The project intends to hire both a technical zoning consultant and a communications consultant to manage outreach.

items.title: Selection Committee and Decision-Making Process
items.summary: The committee discussed the composition of the review team, with members emphasizing that the full City Council and Community Development Board should have an opportunity to review finalists before a selection is finalized. Councilors raised concerns about maintaining legislative authority over zoning decisions relative to appointed boards and the administration.

items.title: RFP Timeline and Deadlines
items.summary: Director Hunt outlined a procurement schedule targeting a mid-February start date, noting that the submission deadline would likely be set for late December or January to avoid holiday conflicts. The council reached a consensus to prioritize a thorough review over an immediate release of the document.

items.title: Amendments to Design Standards and Guidelines
items.summary: Councilors debated whether the inclusion of 'design standards' was too restrictive, leading to an amendment to include 'design guidelines' and a requirement that the consultant analyze how such policies affect project feasibility. The revised scope requires the consultant to work with both boards to determine the best approach for Medford's character.

items.title: Public Engagement and Meeting Requirements
items.summary: The committee compared the proposed public process to previous cycles, discussing a high volume of potential meetings and the risk of public fatigue. Members adjusted the language to allow consultants to propose an effective engagement methodology based on their professional experience rather than adhering to a rigid meeting count.

items.title: Technical Edits and Authorization to Proceed
items.summary: Approved a motion authorizing the Planning Director to move forward with the RFP process after incorporating technical edits regarding contract length, interview protocols, and document summaries. The motion was approved.

items.title: Public Comment
items.summary: Residents spoke in favor of design flexibility, the use of guidelines over rigid standards, and the importance of joint meetings between the City Council and the Community Development Board.
